annotations.label: Metric space

anchor.snippet: a metric space is a set where a notion of distance

annotations.note: Mathlib defines `class MetricSpace` capturing a set with a distance function satisfying the metric axioms.

annotations.label: Formal definition of metric space

anchor.snippet: Formally, a metric space is an ordered pair

annotations.note: Mathlib's `MetricSpace` class encodes the same ordered-pair (M, d) data together with the three metric axioms.

annotations.label: Triangle inequality for a metric

anchor.snippet: ( triangle inequality )

annotations.note: `dist_triangle : dist x z ≤ dist x y + dist y z` is one of the axioms bundled into Mathlib's `PseudoMetricSpace`/`MetricSpace`.

annotations.label: Symmetry of a metric

anchor.snippet: ( symmetry )

annotations.note: `dist_comm : dist x y = dist y x` is Mathlib's symmetry axiom for a (pseudo)metric.

annotations.label: Non-negativity of a metric

anchor.snippet: By taking the third property

annotations.note: `dist_nonneg : 0 ≤ dist x y` is a basic consequence of the (pseudo)metric axioms in `Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean`.

annotations.label: Sequence

anchor.snippet: A sequence is an ordered list

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes sequences both as functions `ℕ → α` (used throughout analysis) and as `Stream'.Seq` for possibly-finite ordered lists.

annotations.label: Convergence of a sequence

anchor.snippet: One of the most important properties of a sequence is convergence

annotations.note: Sequence convergence is expressed via `Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop (𝓝 x)` using Mathlib's filter-based limits.

annotations.label: Continuous function at a point

anchor.snippet: is continuous at a point

annotations.note: `ContinuousAt f x` is defined in Mathlib as `Filter.Tendsto f (𝓝 x) (𝓝 (f x))`.

annotations.label: Continuous function on topological spaces

anchor.snippet: The notion of a continuous function can be generalized to topological spaces

annotations.note: Mathlib's `Continuous f` predicate generalizes continuity to arbitrary topological spaces via the preimage-of-open characterization.

annotations.label: Real analysis

anchor.snippet: Real analysis (traditionally, the "theory of functions of a real variable")

annotations.note: Real analysis is a subject-area label, not a single formal definition; Mathlib develops it in `Mathlib/Analysis/` but does not formalize the meta-notion itself.

annotations.label: Complex analysis

anchor.snippet: Complex analysis (traditionally known as the "theory of functions of a complex variable")

annotations.note: Complex analysis is a discipline name rather than a formal statement; while Mathlib has extensive complex-analysis content, the term itself is not formalized.

annotations.label: Functional analysis

anchor.snippet: Functional analysis is a branch of mathematical analysis

annotations.note: Functional analysis is a subject-area label; Mathlib formalizes its objects (e.g., `NormedSpace`) but not the discipline itself.

annotations.label: Free (noncommutative) analysis

anchor.snippet: Free or noncommutative analysis is a sub-branch of functional analysis

annotations.note: No formalization of free/noncommutative analysis as a topic was found in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Harmonic analysis

anchor.snippet: Harmonic analysis is a branch of mathematical analysis concerned with the representation of functions and signals

annotations.note: Harmonic analysis is a discipline label, not a formal definition; Mathlib has Fourier-analysis content but does not formalize the umbrella term.

annotations.label: Differential equation

anchor.snippet: A differential equation is a mathematical equation for an unknown function

annotations.note: Mathlib's `Mathlib/Analysis/ODE/` formalizes ODE solutions (e.g., Picard–Lindelöf uniqueness), but there is no general `DifferentialEquation` definition.

annotations.label: Measure on a set

anchor.snippet: A measure on a set is a systematic way to assign a number

annotations.note: `MeasureTheory.Measure` is Mathlib's formalization of a measure on a measurable space.

annotations.label: Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space

anchor.snippet: Lebesgue measure on a Euclidean space

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes Lebesgue measure on `ℝ` via the `Real.measureSpace` instance providing `volume : Measure ℝ`, and lifts to `ℝⁿ` via the product Lebesgue measure.

annotations.label: Technical definition of a measure

anchor.snippet: Technically, a measure is a function that assigns a non-negative real number

annotations.note: Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure` encodes the countably-additive non-negative set function with the standard axioms.

annotations.label: σ-algebra of measurable subsets

anchor.snippet: the so-called measurable subsets, which are required to form a

annotations.note: Mathlib's `MeasurableSpace` encodes a σ-algebra: closure of the measurable sets under complements and countable unions/intersections.

annotations.label: Counting measure

anchor.snippet: trivial examples like the counting measure

annotations.note: `MeasureTheory.Measure.count` is Mathlib's formalization of the counting measure on an arbitrary measurable space.

annotations.label: Lebesgue measure of an interval

anchor.snippet: For instance, the Lebesgue measure of the interval

annotations.note: `Real.volume_Ioo`/`volume_Icc` give the Lebesgue measure of an interval as `ENNReal.ofReal (b - a)`.

annotations.label: Numerical analysis

anchor.snippet: Numerical analysis is the study of algorithms that use numerical approximation

annotations.note: Numerical analysis is a subject-area description, not a formal mathematical definition, and is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Vector analysis

anchor.snippet: Vector analysis , also called vector calculus , is a branch of mathematical analysis

annotations.note: Vector analysis is a discipline name; Mathlib has the relevant objects (grad, div, curl-type operators) but not the term itself.

annotations.label: Scalar analysis

anchor.snippet: Scalar analysis is a branch of mathematical analysis dealing with values related to scale

annotations.note: Not a formal mathematical definition; no Mathlib formalization found.

annotations.label: Calculus of variations

anchor.snippet: Calculus of variations deals with extremizing functionals

annotations.note: Calculus of variations is a subject-area label and is not formalized as a definition in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Harmonic analysis (other topics)

anchor.snippet: Harmonic analysis deals with the representation of functions or signals

annotations.note: A duplicate subject-area description; not formalized as a definition in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Geometric analysis

anchor.snippet: Geometric analysis involves the use of geometrical methods

annotations.note: Geometric analysis is a discipline name and is not formalized as such.

annotations.label: Clifford analysis

anchor.snippet: Clifford analysis , the study of Clifford valued functions

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes `CliffordAlgebra` but not Clifford analysis (analytic study of Clifford-valued functions) as a discipline.

annotations.label: p-adic analysis

anchor.snippet: -adic analysis , the study of analysis within the context of

annotations.note: Mathlib defines `Padic` (ℚ_p) and `PadicInt`, providing the setting for p-adic analysis, but p-adic analysis itself is not a formal definition.

annotations.label: Non-standard analysis

anchor.snippet: Non-standard analysis , which investigates the hyperreal numbers

annotations.note: Mathlib has some hyperreals/ultrafilters infrastructure but does not formalize non-standard analysis as a subject.

annotations.label: Computable analysis

anchor.snippet: Computable analysis , the study of which parts of analysis can be carried out

annotations.note: Computable analysis is a subject-area and is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Stochastic calculus

anchor.snippet: Stochastic calculus – analytical notions developed for stochastic processes

annotations.note: Mathlib has probability-theory content but not stochastic calculus as a formalized topic.

annotations.label: Set-valued analysis

anchor.snippet: Set-valued analysis – applies ideas from analysis and topology

annotations.note: Set-valued analysis is a discipline label and is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Convex analysis

anchor.snippet: Convex analysis , the study of convex sets and functions

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes `Convex` sets and `ConvexOn` functions in `Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/`, but not 'convex analysis' as a discipline.

annotations.label: Idempotent analysis

anchor.snippet: Idempotent analysis – analysis in the context of an idempotent semiring

annotations.note: Idempotent analysis is not formalized as a topic in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Constructive analysis

anchor.snippet: Constructive analysis , which is built upon a foundation of constructive

annotations.note: Constructive analysis as a discipline is not formalized in Mathlib (Mathlib uses classical logic).

annotations.label: Intuitionistic analysis

anchor.snippet: Intuitionistic analysis , which is developed from constructive logic

annotations.note: Intuitionistic analysis is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Paraconsistent analysis

anchor.snippet: Paraconsistent analysis , which is built upon a foundation of paraconsistent

annotations.note: Paraconsistent analysis is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Smooth infinitesimal analysis

anchor.snippet: Smooth infinitesimal analysis , which is developed in a smooth topos

annotations.note: Smooth infinitesimal analysis is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Rolle's theorem

anchor.snippet: what is now known as Rolle's theorem

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes Rolle's theorem as `exists_deriv_eq_zero` in `Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LocalExtr.Rolle`: a real-valued function continuous on `[a,b]`, differentiable on `(a,b)`, with `f a = f b` has a point where `f' c = 0`.

annotations.label: Taylor series

anchor.snippet: infinite series expansions, now called Taylor series

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes Taylor polynomials via `taylorWithinEval` and `HasTaylorSeriesUpTo`; the full analytic Taylor-series representation is captured via `FormalMultilinearSeries` and `AnalyticOn`.

annotations.label: Cauchy sequence

anchor.snippet: the concept of the Cauchy sequence

annotations.note: Mathlib defines `CauchySeq u` as `Cauchy (Filter.map u Filter.atTop)`, capturing Cauchy sequences in any uniform space (in particular metric spaces).

annotations.label: (ε, δ)-definition of limit

anchor.snippet: (ε, δ)-definition of limit

annotations.note: The classical ε-δ characterization of limits appears in Mathlib as `Metric.tendsto_nhds` (and its variants for `atTop`, `nhdsWithin`, etc.), providing the ε-δ unfolding of `Filter.Tendsto`.

annotations.label: Baire category theorem

anchor.snippet: Baire category theorem

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes the Baire category theorem via the `BaireSpace` typeclass and the lemma `dense_iInter_of_isOpen`, with instances for complete pseudometric spaces and locally compact regular spaces.

annotations.label: Lebesgue integration

anchor.snippet: Lebesgue integration

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes the Lebesgue integral (as the Bochner integral of Banach-space-valued functions) as `MeasureTheory.integral`, notation `∫ x, f x ∂μ`.

annotations.label: Hilbert space

anchor.snippet: Hilbert spaces

annotations.note: A Hilbert space in Mathlib is a complete `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E`, i.e. `InnerProductSpace` together with `[CompleteSpace E]`; there is no single dedicated `HilbertSpace` typeclass.

annotations.label: Normed vector space

anchor.snippet: The idea of normed vector space

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes normed vector spaces as `NormedSpace 𝕜 E`, layered over `NormedAddCommGroup E` and a `NormedField 𝕜`.

annotations.label: Analytic function

anchor.snippet: the analytic functions of complex variables

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes analyticity as `AnalyticAt`/`AnalyticOn`: locally expressible as a convergent power series via `FormalMultilinearSeries`.

annotations.label: Meromorphic function

anchor.snippet: meromorphic functions

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes meromorphic functions as `MeromorphicAt`/`MeromorphicOn`, defined via analyticity of `(z - z₀)^n • f`.

annotations.label: Fourier transform

anchor.snippet: Fourier transform

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes the Fourier transform generally as `VectorFourier.fourierIntegral` (on locally compact abelian groups with an additive character), with the standard Fourier transform on ℝⁿ obtained by specialization.

annotations.label: Fourier series

anchor.snippet: Fourier series

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes Fourier series on the circle via `fourierCoeff` (Fourier coefficients on `AddCircle T`) with L²-completeness results.

annotations.label: Dedekind cuts (construction of ℝ)

anchor.snippet: constructed the real numbers by Dedekind cuts

annotations.note: Mathlib constructs `Real` as the completion of `ℚ` via Cauchy sequences rather than Dedekind cuts; the Dedekind-cut construction itself is not the definition used, though the resulting ordered field is the same.

annotations.label: Method of exhaustion

anchor.snippet: used the method of exhaustion to compute the area and volume

annotations.note: The method of exhaustion is a historical proof technique; individual area/volume computations are formalized in Mathlib but the method itself is not a formal definition.

annotations.label: Cavalieri's principle

anchor.snippet: would later be called Cavalieri's principle

annotations.note: The general Cavalieri's principle relating volumes of solids with equal cross-sectional areas does not appear as a named theorem in Mathlib, though special integration-based volume equalities are provable.

annotations.label: Cartesian coordinate system

anchor.snippet: introduced the Cartesian coordinate system

annotations.note: Mathlib models Cartesian coordinates via `Fin n → ℝ` and the inner-product structure on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`; the abstract 'coordinate system' concept itself is not defined.

annotations.label: Mathematical function

anchor.snippet: Euler introduced the notion of a mathematical function

annotations.note: Functions are a primitive of Lean 4's type theory (`α → β`); Mathlib's `Function` namespace supplies the standard operations and lemmas.

annotations.label: Riemann integration

anchor.snippet: the theorems of Riemann integration

annotations.note: Mathlib does not define the Riemann integral directly; it uses the Bochner integral, with `intervalIntegral` playing the role of the (definite) Riemann integral for continuous or interval-integrable functions.

annotations.label: Axiom of choice

anchor.snippet: a non-trivial consequence of the axiom of choice

annotations.note: The axiom of choice is available in Lean/Mathlib as `Classical.choice`; the existence of Lebesgue non-measurable sets (Vitali sets) has been formalized using it.

annotations.label: Differentiable manifold

anchor.snippet: Differentiable manifolds

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes smooth/differentiable manifolds via `ChartedSpace` plus `IsManifold I n M` (formerly `SmoothManifoldWithCorners`) parameterized by a model with corners and smoothness class.

annotations.label: Partial differential equation

anchor.snippet: Partial differential equations

annotations.note: Mathlib has scattered results involving specific PDEs (e.g., Laplace's equation) but no general formalization of PDEs as a class.

annotations.label: Analytic number theory

anchor.snippet: Analytic number theory

annotations.note: Analytic number theory is a subject-area label; Mathlib has significant analytic-number-theory content (Dirichlet series, PNT progress) but the discipline itself is not a formal definition.

annotations.label: Hyperreal numbers

anchor.snippet: the hyperreal numbers

annotations.note: Mathlib defines `Hyperreal` as the ultraproduct `Germ (hyperfilter ℕ) ℝ`, providing the setting for non-standard analysis.
